title: arXiv Mathematics — 13 November 2026: 9 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-recent-paper ordering, not measured popularity. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old.

sections.title: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
sections.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body in R^n, the authors claim a volume-preserving linear image containing a near-copy with isoperimetric quotient at most 40 epsilon^-1 sqrt(n), resolving Naor's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and introduction claim that for every origin-symmetric convex body K there is T in SL_n(R) such that for every 0<epsilon<1 some origin-symmetric L satisfies (1-epsilon)TK subset L subset TK and iq(L)<=40 epsilon^-1 sqrt(n). Setting epsilon=1/2 gives the stated conjecture resolution.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite-dimensional real space; K is an origin-symmetric convex body and the linear map preserves volume.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound worsens as the allowed relative approximation epsilon shrinks; the abstract establishes an existence theorem, not a result for nonsymmetric bodies.

sections.title: Hilbert’s 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
sections.abstract: The authors prove undecidability of nonnegativity for rational symmetric functions across all dimensions and exhibit a positive-definite degree-8 symmetric function with no sum-of-squares multiplier uniform in dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and introduction claim that deciding whether a rational-coefficient symmetric function is nonnegative in every dimension is undecidable, even for homogeneous functions in Q[p2,p4,...,p46]; they also give a homogeneous degree-8 positive-definite example with no multiplier yielding sums of squares uniformly in dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nonnegative in every dimension means every finite-variable truncation is nonnegative; the decision problem is over rational-coefficient symmetric functions. The counterexample is positive definite in each finite dimension but rules out a bounded-degree uniform sum-of-squares multiplier.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note another manuscript independently settles the undecidability case, creating priority/overlap for that result; their uniform-certificate counterexample is a separate contribution.

sections.title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
sections.abstract: For every unbounded subset A of R and every 0<epsilon<1, the author constructs a closed set occupying at least 1-epsilon of every unit interval yet containing no nontrivial affine copy of A.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and Theorem 1.2 claim a closed symmetric S with measure at least 1-epsilon in every unit interval, avoiding all nontrivial affine copies of any given unbounded A; every such affine copy misses S in infinitely many points.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The forbidden pattern A is any unbounded subset of the real line; large means uniform lower density in every interval of length one, not merely positive global density.
sections.unique_caveat: The introduction distinguishes this strengthened-density question from the original Erdős similarity conjecture for positive-measure sets, which it says remains open in general.

sections.title: The Brown–Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
sections.abstract: The authors construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space with radial zero set of logarithmic capacity zero whose polynomial multiples fail to approximate the constant function, contradicting the Brown–Shields conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims noncyclicity despite outerness and polar radial zero set, and says every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated by such counterexamples in the Dirichlet norm and L1 norm of boundary logarithms.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Analytic Dirichlet space on the unit disk; the zero set is defined by radial limits on the unit circle, with logarithmic capacity zero.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors label this an expository version with navigational aids, not intended for publication; the claimed refutation remains a preprint result pending independent scrutiny.

sections.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős–Graham irregularity problem
sections.abstract: The author gives explicit asymptotics and multiple limit points for the largest subset of {1,...,floor(cn)} avoiding a distinct-element sum of n, and proves an inverse theorem for dense sets with forbidden sums.
sections.claimed_result: For c>=1, f_c(n)=floor(cn)-ceil(n/2); for 0<c<1, f_c(n)/n does not converge, with at least two limit points and arbitrarily many as c approaches 0 or 1. The inverse theorem forces a subset summing to sT under stated density and range hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f_c(n) maximizes the size of A subset {1,...,floor(cn)} with no subset of distinct elements summing to n. The inverse theorem uses the least positive q not dividing s and the abstract's bound on E for sufficiently large T.
sections.unique_caveat: Lean formalization covers the c>=1 result, limsup, and limit/inverse-theorem cases q in {2,3} described in the abstract; it does not certify the entire theorem suite.

sections.title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
sections.abstract: For complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from one real Gaussian field on the circle, the author proves the conjectured Fourier-dimension formula throughout the stated parameter range and gives boundary and Sobolev regularity results.
sections.claimed_result: For the canonical holomorphic family, the abstract states that Fourier dimension at gamma=alpha+i beta equals real-chaos dimension at alpha minus beta squared almost surely on the open unit disk and the stated region 1/sqrt(2)<|alpha|<sqrt(2), |alpha|+|beta|<sqrt(2); it describes separate boundary behavior.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complex chaos is built from one real Gaussian field on the circle; the almost-sure simultaneous assertion applies to the canonical holomorphic family and the parameter regions stated in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is circle-specific and parameter-dependent; the abstract gives separate boundary behavior and does not claim the identity outside its stated range.

sections.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
sections.abstract: For stationary Poissonian log-correlated fields generated by an analytic periodic function, the authors derive a high-probability maximum asymptotic with random-time fluctuation and logarithmic correction.
sections.claimed_result: For centered 1-periodic analytic f, the authors claim with high probability max over [-1,1] X_n(t)=c1 n+c2 tau_n-(c3+o(1))log n, with positive constants depending on f; Poisson arrival times yield fluctuations of order sqrt(n).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: X_n(t)=sum_{j<=n} f(exp(tau_j)t+v_j), with rate-one Poisson arrival times tau_j and independent uniform v_j in [0,1).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors conjecture analogous asymptotics for random permutation matrix characteristic polynomials; that extension is not proved here.

sections.title: Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels
sections.abstract: For finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel, the authors prove mean-field passage-time and Gaussian hopcount limits, plus a Markov-chain approximation to the geodesic.
sections.claimed_result: Under a uniform absolute spectral gap and an O(N^-1) bound on a fixed even-step return probability, the authors claim the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit, an independent Gaussian hopcount limit, and total-variation approximation of the geodesic by an independent Markov chain stopped at that hopcount.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite weighted graphs on N vertices; normalized Weibull edge hazards define a symmetric Markov kernel satisfying the stated spectral-gap and return-probability bounds, with edge-law perturbations within the abstract's relative hazard error condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The limiting conclusions depend on the kernel hypotheses; the abstract does not claim universality for arbitrary graph sequences or edge-weight distributions.

sections.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
sections.abstract: For the focusing energy-critical wave equation in three dimensions, the authors construct a bounded forward-global solution near a sign-changing stationary state whose asymptotic stationary core cannot be represented by one fixed profile.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct a bounded forward-global solution starting arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state, asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave, with two limits in distinct similarity orbits; this contradicts fixed-profile resolution.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional focusing energy-critical quintic wave equation; the construction is near a particular sign-changing stationary state and uses summable radiation packets.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample is specific to the stated equation and profile regime; validation includes a computer-assisted certificate whose details and proof remain for specialist scrutiny.
